headline: 0 addresses catalogued: XRPL DEX is a protocol-native order book and AMM on the XRP Ledger, with no deployed-contracts registry found.

findings.text: No EVM-style block-explorer name-tag search applies. The only chain is the XRP Ledger. The explorer list on xrpl.org (Ripple's livenet.xrpl.org, Bithomp, XRPScan, XRPLWin, RWA.xyz, XRPL.to) was recorded. The livenet.xrpl.org fetch returned only a 'enable JavaScript' shell, so no addresses were extracted.

No 'deployed contracts' or addresses page was found for the XRPL DEX. The DEX docs describe offers (limit orders) and AMMs as ledger-native objects, not deployed contracts, so protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc is left null.
No audit links were pinned for this protocol, and none were found on the pages walked. There is nothing to extract from audit scope tables.

The XRPLF GitHub org page was fetched and lists rippled (the C++ server implementing the XRP Ledger protocol) plus xrpl-dev-portal, which holds the docs source. The rippled repo itself was not fetchable in this run, so no deployment artifacts or commit SHA were pinned. No deployment artifacts are expected, because the DEX is part of the ledger protocol rather than a deployed contract.
Only one chain (the XRP Ledger, listed as Ripple) is in scope. There is no multi-chain enumeration to do.

There is no factory contract. The AMM docs say each AMM is a ledger entry plus a special AccountRoot whose address is chosen somewhat randomly at creation. The AMM docs also say there is at most one AMM per asset pair. Order books are tracked on demand per currency pair. No enumeration view was available through the read API, which only supports EVM chains. This is recorded as an enumeration gap, not a cap.
No addresses were catalogued, so no role taxonomy was applied.
admin_addresses is empty. No address was surfaced from a fetched URL, and none was taken from memory.

rationale.verdict: Walked xrpl.org home, DEX and AMM concept docs, the explorers page, the XRPLF GitHub org and a 2020 rippled release post; catalogued 0 addresses because the DEX is a protocol-native feature with no named contract or registry.

evidence.shows: Capability probe of protocol.website succeeded. The site describes XRP Ledger as a Layer 1 blockchain with built-in trading (DEX, permissioned DEX, AMM). It says developers can 'skip complex smart contract development'. It links to docs, explorers, known amendments and the XRPLF GitHub org. No contract address table is present.

The DEX is a native order book of Offers (limit orders), operating since 2012. Trading pairs are tracked on demand, and trades are made by sending transactions (OfferCreate/OfferCancel). The page lists no deployed addresses.

AMMs are ledger entries: an AMM entry, a special AccountRoot (address chosen somewhat randomly at creation, different if re-created) and trust lines. There is at most one AMM per asset pair. LP token holders vote on the trading fee, 0% to 1%. The page lists no fixed addresses.
Lists XRPL explorers by operator: Ripple (livenet.xrpl.org), Bithomp, XRPScan, XRPLWin, RWA.xyz and XRPL.to.
Ripple's XRPL explorer returned only a JavaScript-required shell. No on-chain data was extractable by this fetch tool (failed on-chain probe).
The XRPLF org lists rippled (C++ daemon implementing the XRP Ledger protocol, ISC license) and xrpl-dev-portal (source for xrpl.org docs). It also lists clio and XRPL-Standards.

A 2020 release post pointing to Ripple's bug bounty program at https://ripple.com/bug-bounty/. It also describes the amendment process (protocol changes after two weeks of >80% support from trusted validators). The bounty reference is dated and the link itself was not fetched.

unknowns: D1: XRPL explorers were not usable. livenet.xrpl.org returned only a JavaScript shell. Bithomp, XRPScan, XRPLWin and XRPL.to were not fetched because the fetch budget ran out. No name-tagged addresses were surfaced.
D1-offchain: The on-chain explorer fetch (https://livenet.xrpl.org/) failed to return ledger data. Evidence is off-chain docs only.
D2: No deployed-contracts / addresses page was found for the XRPL DEX. The DEX appears to have no per-protocol deployment, but a page that was not fetched could exist.
D3: No audit_links were pinned and none were found on the pages walked. No audit scope addresses were extracted.
D4: The https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled repo was not fetchable (not previously surfaced to the fetch tool as a URL). No commit SHA was pinned and no deployment artifacts were examined.
D5: chain Ripple: zero addresses surfaced from xrpl.org docs, the XRPLF GitHub org page and the livenet explorer shell.

D6: AMM pseudo-account addresses and order-book directory entries are not enumerable via the defipunkd read API, which supports EVM chains only. AMM and order-book enumeration would need XRPL RPC (amm_info, book_offers, ledger_data) or an explorer index. There is no factory to cap.
D7: No addresses were found, so no roles were assigned. Any XRPL-specific control surface, such as the validator list or amendment voting, was not mapped to addresses.
D8: No snippet-only address sightings were recorded, and none were fabricated.

D4: protocol_metadata.upgradeability left unknown. Protocol changes happen via validator-voted amendments, which is not a proxy-style upgrade pattern, and a more precise classification was not determined.
D2: bug_bounty_url (https://ripple.com/bug-bounty/) is cited only through a 2020 release post and was not fetched directly. It may be stale.
D2: governance_forum, voting_token and security_contact were not verified this run.

protocol_metadata.about: The XRPL DEX is the XRP Ledger's built-in exchange. Users place Offers (limit orders) to trade XRP and issued tokens, and a trade may match offers, AMM pools or both. The ledger also hosts constant-product-style AMM pools, where liquidity providers hold LP tokens and vote on the trading fee. Trading is done by sending ledger transactions, with no separately deployed smart contracts.
